newsitem.title: GERMANY: German aluminium foil orders up in early 1997.
newsitem.headline: German aluminium foil orders up in early 1997.

text.p: German aluminium industry association GDA said orders for foil and narrow strip in January 1997 were up 20 percent on a year earlier, and the trend was maintained in February.
Export sales in 1997 should be boosted by the strong dollar, Armin Weinhold, chairman of GDA's foil and strip division, said in a statement.
Dollar strength brought currency-related cost advantages of up to 20 percent in certain foil producing countries, he said.
Some of the 21 member companies in the GDA division were investing in capacity in the U.S., China, Southeast Asia and Poland.
"This strengthens our position in the increasingly globalised market," Weinhold said.
Output by the 21 companies in 1996 dropped by three percent over 1995 to 188,000 tonnes.
Sales revenue declined to 2.07 billion marks from 2.15 billion a year earlier.
Weinhold cited weaker demand for aluminium from food and drinks retailers and a sharp decline in building industry activity for the losses in 1996.
Domestic sales were down 2.8 percent at 62,700 tonnes.
The share of imports in domestic demand exceeded 50 percent.
Exports, which accounted for more than 65 percent of GDA members' sales, were down four percent at 125,000 tonnes.
Weinhold said the industry was betting on exports because the domestic environment was hostile to its activities.
The industry had built up costly recycling facilities and achieved a high recycling rate of 70 percent, but some politicians were still calling for a ban on aluminium packaging.
A trend towards lighter products was reducing specific aluminium uses in domestic applications.
